items.title: The UK’s @AISecurityInst (AISI) has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of A...
items.content:
The UK’s @AISecurityInst (AISI) has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The models attempted to complete an assignment in a setup where their normal safeguards were removed and they were deliberately given internet access. AISI reports that the models “engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations”.

We’re grateful to AISI for their leadership in the important discussion about how to evaluate increasingly capable AI agents. We’re working closely with them to gather more details of the incident as we conduct our own investigation. Gaining a clear picture of Claude’s understanding of its situation—by examining its reasoning transcripts and running our own analyses—will help us identify the causes of its behavior.

The prompts in the evaluation did not impose any specific restrictions on how the internet should be used. This and the removal of safeguards meant that the models were tested under “deliberately permissive conditions” that are not representative of any of our production models. Note that there was no evidence here of an escape from a secure environment.

AISI’s disclosure of the incident can be found here: https://t.co/cJ3hCBtBU7

items.title: In case you were wondering why Apple removed Telegram from the App Store. Basically, it was removed ...
items.content:
In case you were wondering why Apple removed Telegram from the App Store. Basically, it was removed for about 40 minutes and then restored.

The reason for the removal is curious, though. There are people creating bots that automatically post child abuse content in legitimate public groups and demand ransom from the owners of these groups to stop doing that.

If the owner refuses, the extortionists flood those public groups with illegal content and then report these groups directly to Apple.

Because Apple maintains a zero-tolerance protocol for this specific category of illegal material, their system automatically pulled the app to prevent further distribution, bypassed standard joint notices, and flagged the issue to Telegram afterward.

Basically, it's a way to ruin any app with user-generated content unless they pay ransom or are seriously lawyered up, like Telegram.

items.title: In 1930, the Spanish philosopher José Ortega y Gasset published The Revolt of the Masses, a book tha...
items.content:
In 1930, the Spanish philosopher José Ortega y Gasset published The Revolt of the Masses, a book that still reads as prophetic. His chief target was not the poor or the working class, but a new type of person he called "mass man."

Mass man, in Ortega's view, is defined by an attitude toward life rather than by income. He is the ordinary person who is thoroughly pleased with himself, who demands nothing further of his own character or intellect, and who nevertheless insists that his mediocrity be treated as a right. He does not bow before excellence, competence, or higher standards. He regards them with suspicion or resentment. What in earlier times was considered the privilege of the few—political influence, cultural authority, the right to shape society—mass man now takes as his own, without making any effort to rise above the average.

Ortega believed this human type was produced by the very success of modern civilization. Rising living standards, mass education, and liberal institutions gave ordinary people extraordinary power and comfort. But they did not develop a corresponding sense of responsibility or humility before higher achievement. The result was a revolt: the common man refused to acknowledge the authority of superior knowledge, culture, or character. He demanded that everything be brought down to his own level.

The danger, Ortega warned, was that a civilization cannot survive if its central actors no longer respect the standards that made it possible. When the average comes to dominate while aspiring to nothing beyond itself, excellence is undermined, institutions decay, and politics becomes an expression of resentment rather than of responsibility.
